The advance is now a route to thermal-state access

I pursued the stronger opening: can the acquired representation support the constraints needed to construct a quantum thermal state, while keeping the interacting computation explicit and fully paid?

The answer is yes for the promised class, with three distinct results:

A proved inner solver: the bulk and fast temporal coordinates admit an explicit Gaussian/path Gibbs update with a convergence bound independent of the temporal mesh. A finite annealed-importance certificate computes their normalizer without assuming equilibrium at every intermediate step.
A completed classical computation: the full high-frequency method now runs on an acquired, connected, frustrated input. It computes the physical log normalizer to certified error below 
0.03
0.03, including acquisition, temporal approximation, quadrature, sampling and numerical costs.
A proved state-preparation consequence: the construction survives exact spin constraints at selected imaginary-time slices. Those constrained normalizers supply an established quantum Gibbs-state preparation method. I also proved a sharp precision bound for that interface.

The general state-preparation algorithm remains a theorem; no quantum circuit was executed. The native classical implementation covers the recorded rank-one model with a connected cycle bulk and one retained static coordinate. Direct spectral computation wins decisively on that small input. The consequential result is the broader capability and its constructive cost, rather than a performance claim for the fixture.

The complete synthesis is in 
MAIN_THEOREM.md
, with the evidence, failures and preserved predecessor work indexed in 
RESEARCH_RECORD.md
.

## What materially changed

P3 has converted its field-uniform high-frequency covariance bound into an explicit conditional algorithm. For acquired `J = D0 + S + AA^T`, with `S` positive semidefinite of norm at most kappa and bounded-rank collective `AA^T` of norm at most Lambda, the contraction premise is `alpha = kappa chi_M + 4 Lambda/Omega < 1`. Alternating Gaussian augmentation and independent whole-spin cyclic-path updates have claimed spectral gap at least `1-alpha` and relative-entropy contraction at most alpha. This removes time-mesh size from the number of sweeps needed for contraction. Every sweep still pays for every bulk/fast coordinate and all time slices; total runtime is not mesh-independent.

The normalizer construction now has an explicit AIS second-moment bound using invariant intermediate kernels, without presuming intermediate equilibrium. The extensive refinement bounds energy variance by O(n) at fixed physical parameters and supports an O(n)-stage schedule. The completed small execution uses the earlier range-based schedule instead; the stronger extensive constants are less attractive on that fixture. Refining an AIS grid alone does not repair an identity kernel, as the retained counterexample demonstrates.

The thermal-state consequence earns a previously missing closure property: arbitrary compatible longitudinal pins preserve the covariance premise and tractable conditional path calculation. It uses the correct potential-outside symmetric product. Equality of unpinned traces does not imply equality of pinned probabilities. The operator-log error and mesh bounds distinguish bounded row strength from bounded spectral norms; the latter can require the more conservative O(n/sqrt(epsilon)) physical mesh.

P3 also obtains a sharp interface bound for positive prefix-mass estimates. With `m` bits and multiplicative log error eta, the resulting state error is at most `2 sqrt(1-sech(eta/2)^(2m)) <= sqrt(m) eta`. A product construction attains the order of this dependence. This improves the precision requirement for this particular prefix interface. It is not a lower bound against every state-preparation method. A frozen random tape and amplification accommodate all coherent prefixes with polynomial overhead, provided numerical errors receive the same stringent allocation. Quantum gates, reversible computation and a high-precision pinned count
